findings.problem: TelemetryWorkflow uses primitive String for status and bool flags (is_validated, is_sent) instead of enums or typestates, allowing illegal states like validated=false and is_sent=true simultaneously
findings.failure_mode: Any combination of status/is_validated/is_sent is constructible at compile time; the business invariant that telemetry must be validated before being sent is enforced by no code and cannot be checked by the type system
findings.fix: Replace status, is_validated, and is_sent with a single TelemetryState enum (e.g., Pending, Validated, Sent) and remove the primitive fields entirely

findings.problem: id is a plain pub String with no domain semantics; status is a plain pub String that should be an enum variant or state machine field
findings.failure_mode: Any arbitrary string is accepted as an ID or status, including empty strings, null-like values, or values that violate domain invariants; no compile-time guarantee that id is well-formed or status is valid
findings.fix: Introduce a TelemetryId newtype wrapping String (or [u8; N] if fixed-size) with a fallible constructor, and replace status String with a typed TelemetryState enum

findings.problem: All fields of TelemetryWorkflow are pub, allowing external code to mutate any field directly and bypass any invariants
findings.failure_mode: Callers can set is_sent=true and is_validated=false simultaneously, or set status to an arbitrary string, without going through mark_sent or any state-transition function
findings.fix: Make all fields private and provide a sealed constructor; expose only state-transition methods that enforce invariants

findings.problem: mark_sent mutates item in-place by reassigning fields rather than returning a new state; it does not check preconditions (e.g., is_validated must be true) before allowing the sent transition
findings.failure_mode: Telemetry can be marked sent without ever being validated, violating the domain workflow invariant; in-place mutation obscures the state transition and enables stale-state bugs in concurrent or async contexts
findings.fix: Change mark_sent to a fallible method or constructor that takes &self (or Self) and returns Result<Self, TransitionError>, checking that the source state allows a transition to Sent

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms is Option<u64> with no domain typing or validation; a raw u64 epoch provides no compile-time guarantees about validity or interpretation
findings.failure_mode: Callers can store arbitrary u64 values (zero, overflow, non-epoch values) as the sent timestamp; no domain-level validation or conversion to human-readable form is guaranteed by the type
findings.fix: Introduce a SentAt newtype or use chrono/time crate types, or at minimum make it a private field set only by the state-transition method that records the actual epoch

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms is u64 but no conversion or range validation is present; if this value is used in arithmetic (e.g., duration calculations, comparison with system clock), unchecked arithmetic could overflow
findings.failure_mode: If sent_at_epoch_ms is used in arithmetic downstream, overflow or underflow can produce incorrect time differences silently
findings.fix: Use checked arithmetic for any operations on sent_at_epoch_ms, or store it as a typed duration/timestamp type that enforces checked operations at the type level

findings.problem: mark_sent allocates a new String via "sent".to_string() on every call instead of using a zero-copy enum variant or &'static str reference
findings.failure_mode: Every mark_sent call heap-allocates a String for the literal "sent", adding unnecessary allocation pressure in what should be a hot path for telemetry processing
findings.fix: Replace the String status field with a TelemetryState enum variant TelemetryState::Sent that carries zero heap allocation; only allocate when transitioning from external input

findings.problem: The struct and function together form a single module with no separation between data (calculations) and actions; there is no boundary between pure domain logic and I/O shell
findings.failure_mode: No clear separation makes it impossible to unit-test the core domain logic independently of I/O; future additions of serialization, persistence, or network logic risk polluting the pure core
findings.fix: Split into a pure TelemetryDomain module (typestates, state transitions, invariants) and an ImperativeShell module (serialization, persistence, network send)

findings.problem: mark_sent returns TelemetryWorkflow directly with no error type; if preconditions (validation) must be enforced, there is no mechanism to signal failure
findings.failure_mode: Invalid state transitions are silently allowed or must be silently ignored; callers have no way to detect that a transition was rejected or that the telemetry was not in a valid pre-transition state
findings.fix: Change mark_sent to return Result<TelemetryWorkflow, TransitionError> where TransitionError is an enum covering InvalidStateTransition and similar domain errors

findings.problem: "sent".to_string() uses String::from which could panic on OOM; while OOM is rare, the Holzman Rust contract requires allocation-aware code with try_reserve or fallible allocation paths
findings.failure_mode: In resource-constrained environments, the allocation of "sent" could fail, causing a panic rather than a graceful error return
findings.fix: Use an enum-based state representation to eliminate the allocation entirely, or use fallible allocation if the String field must be retained

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent or any throughput/latency claim
no profiler data or allocation analysis (e.g., criterion, flamegraph, or valgrind) for the telemetry workflow hot path
no allocation audit: mark_sent allocates a String per call without try_reserve or zero-copy optimization
no second-ring evidence: no behavior tests, integration tests, or external test files exist
no command evidence: no cargo test, cargo fmt, or cargo clippy output reported
residual_risk: The codebase has fundamental architectural violations: illegal states are fully representable via primitive fields, no typestate enforcement exists, mark_sent allows invalid state transitions without preconditions, and all fields are publicly mutable. The absence of any tests means there is no behavioral contract to validate fixes. Static review only — no commands run.
